title: The value-fallback prettifier `humanizeLabel` has two byte-identical copies and disagrees with the key-fallback convention on camelCase input
body:
Recorded while implementing objectui#5425 (the rendering half of objectstack#10292). Filed unassigned, as an observation — no user-visible two-spelling defect reproduces from it today.

## What is there

The renderer carries two *separate* "prettify a machine string for display" conventions, and one of them has no single home.

**Key fallback** (a field key becomes a column header) — one implementation, and its docstring says so:

- `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/utils.ts` — `humanizeFieldKey`, "Single home for the convention, because both halves of the `table` widget family need it and they must agree". Maps `_` to a space, splits camelCase, title-cases.

**Value fallback** (a stored value becomes a display string when nothing resolves it) — two byte-identical copies:

- `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — `humanizeLabel`, read by `plugin-grid`, `plugin-gantt`, `plugin-detail`
- `packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx` — `humanizeLabel`, a deliberate local copy whose comment says "Local implementation to avoid a dependency on `@object-ui/fields`"

The two conventions disagree, because the value copy does not split camelCase. Measured by running all of them over one input set:

```
input                humanizeFieldKey     humanizeLabel
needs_analysis       Needs Analysis       Needs Analysis
NeedsAnalysis        Needs Analysis       NeedsAnalysis      <-- differ
unitPrice            Unit Price           UnitPrice          <-- differ
BestCase             Best Case            BestCase           <-- differ
lost-to-competitor   Lost-To-Competitor   Lost To Competitor <-- differ
```

That top-right pair is exactly the two spellings objectstack#10292 measured on a 17.1.0 dashboard (`NeedsAnalysis` on the bar axis, `Needs Analysis` in the pivot row label). It is recorded here as provenance, not as a live reproduction: on current `main` a dataset dimension member reaches neither function — it resolves through the picklist field's declared options and the locale bundle, and otherwise renders as stored. Pinned in `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DatasetWidget.dimensionMemberLabels.test.tsx`.

## Why it was not fixed under objectui#5425

Aligning the value fallback with the key convention means changing both copies together. Changing only the `plugin-charts` one would trade a latent disagreement for a live one: a chart's free-form member would read `Unit Price` while a grid's option fallback over the same string read `UnitPrice`. `packages/fields` was outside that card's declared file surface and was held by another in-flight claim (PR #5441) at the time, so the change was left whole rather than half-made.

## What a fix would look like

One implementation of the value fallback, reachable from both `packages/fields` and `packages/plugin-charts` — `@object-ui/core` is the only shared ancestor, and objectui#4389 already ruled that direction for this family ("core-canonical logic, plugins consume; never core importing react"). Whether it should then *converge* with `humanizeFieldKey` is a separate question: they take different inputs (a declared key vs. an arbitrary stored value), so keeping them distinct may be correct — but if so, that distinction should be written down, because today it reads as drift.

Also worth deciding in the same pass: the dataset path prettifies free-form members not at all, while the object-bound chart path applies `humanizeLabel` to them. One dashboard can hold both bindings.

## Duplicate search

Searched `objectstack-ai/objectui` issues before filing, each term separately:

- "humanizeLabel duplicated between plugin-charts and fields, prettifier has no single home" — 4 hits, all unrelated (#5425 itself, #4389, #4405, #4401)
- "humanizeLabel duplicate copy packages/fields" — 3 hits, all unrelated (#4788, #3910, #2260)
- "free-form dimension value fallback prettifier camelCase not split PascalCase" — 0 hits

Nothing covers the duplication or the disagreement.
